content.overview: Section 168 provides that a director may resign from office by giving notice in writing to the company. The Board must take note of the resignation, and the company must intimate the Registrar and place the fact of resignation in the report of directors laid in the immediately following general meeting. The director must also forward a copy of the resignation with reasons to the Registrar within the prescribed time. Resignation takes effect from the date on which the notice is received by the company or the date specified by the director in the notice, whichever is later. Resignation does not absolve the director from liabilities in respect of the period of office.
content.glance: Written notice to company; Board notes; company intimates ROC and reports to next GM; director also files with ROC; effective on later of receipt or specified date; liabilities for tenure remain.
content.study: A director may resign from his office by giving a notice in writing to the company and the Board shall on receipt of such notice take note of the same and the company shall intimate the Registrar in such manner, within such time and in such form as may be prescribed and shall also place the fact of such resignation in the report of directors laid in the immediately following general meeting by the company. A director shall also forward a copy of his resignation along with detailed reasons for the resignation to the Registrar within such time as may be prescribed. The resignation shall take effect from the date on which the notice is received by the company or the date, if any, specified by the director in the notice, whichever is later. The director who has resigned shall be liable even after his resignation for the offences which occurred during his tenure. Current-law framing: confirm written notice; fix effective date; check Board note, company ROC filing and director’s own ROC filing; note continuing liability for tenure acts.

sections.heading: Notice
sections.body: Director gives written notice of resignation to the company.

sections.heading: Board and Company Duties
sections.body: Board takes note; company intimates the Registrar and places the fact in the directors’ report at the next general meeting.

sections.heading: Director’s Filing
sections.body: Director also forwards a copy of the resignation with reasons to the Registrar within the prescribed time.

sections.heading: Effective Date
sections.body: Later of the date the company receives the notice or the date specified in the notice.

sections.heading: Continuing Liability
sections.body: Resignation does not relieve the director of liability for offences or acts during the period of office.

examples.title: Effective date
examples.body: A director’s notice is received by the company on 1 March and specifies 15 March as the resignation date. Under s. 168 the resignation takes effect on 15 March.

examples.title: Liability after resignation
examples.body: A director resigns in June. An offence arising from acts in April remains attributable to that director for the tenure period despite the later resignation.

hypotheticals.question: Can the Board refuse to accept a valid written resignation?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 168 provides that a director may resign by written notice; the Board takes note and the company and director complete the prescribed filings. The statute does not condition resignation on Board ‘acceptance’ as a separate power to refuse a valid notice.

distinctions.title: Resignation (s. 168) vs vacation (s. 167) vs removal (s. 169)
distinctions.left: Voluntary written notice by the director
distinctions.right: Vacation is automatic on statutory grounds; removal is by members’ ordinary resolution after special notice

misconceptions.trap: Resignation wipes out all liability for past acts as director.
misconceptions.correction: Section 168 expressly preserves liability for offences which occurred during the tenure.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 168 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm written notice. II. Fix effective date (later of receipt or specified date). III. Check Board note and ROC filings. IV. Note continuing tenure liability. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Notice facts; effective date; filing status; liability period; precise relief.

examTips: Effective date = later of receipt or specified date.
Director and company both file with ROC.
